facts.raw_span: a 4-week history of a rapidly growing left caruncular lesion
an amelanotic, pedunculated mass with an ulcerated surface, arising from the caruncle
no evidence of PAM (primary acquired melanosis)
The specimen measured 8 × 6 × 5 mm and had a 4-mm ulceration with necrotic tissue on its surface
Revealed a solid tumor with an inflamed crust on its surface, composed of large anaplastic cells with mitotic activity
Showed positive reactivity to melanocytic markers HMB45, MITF2, and Melan-A
The Ki-67 proliferation marker showed a significant number of cycling cells
Sentinel lymph node biopsy findings were negative
Conjunctival and orbital biopsies revealed no tumor
Ulcerated, pedunculated, caruncular tumor
Mitotically active tumor containing anaplastic epithelioid cells
Melanoma cells showing immunoreactivity for Melan-A

concepts.why: The presence of a rapidly growing, ulcerated, and pedunculated mass with anaplastic cells and positive reactivity to melanocytic markers supports this diagnosis.
The amelanotic nature of the tumor, combined with positive reactivity to melanocytic markers, supports this diagnosis.
The Ki-67 proliferation marker showed a significant number of cycling cells, indicating a high proliferative index.
Sentinel lymph node biopsy findings were negative and conjunctival and orbital biopsies revealed no tumor, indicating the melanoma is localized.

rationales.F01: Rapid growth of the lesion suggests malignancy
rationales.F02: Amelanotic and pedunculated mass is characteristic of amelanotic melanoma
rationales.F05: Anaplastic cells with mitotic activity indicate high-grade melanoma
rationales.F06: Positive reactivity to melanocytic markers confirms melanoma
rationales.F07: High Ki-67 proliferation index indicates aggressive tumor behavior
rationales.F11: Mitotically active tumor with anaplastic epithelioid cells is diagnostic of high-grade melanoma
rationales.F12: Immunoreactivity for Melan-A confirms melanoma cells

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of an amelanotic, pedunculated mass with an ulcerated surface arising from the caruncle, along with positive reactivity to melanocytic markers and significant mitotic activity, strongly supports the diagnosis of Malignant melanoma of the caruncle.
